primitives.name: DST Offense Matchup Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: Worst offenses faced by slate DSTs: TB faces CLE (20.1), SF faces MIA (25.6), PHI faces TEN (26.0), CAR faces ATL (44.2)...
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{\\text{dst}}': 'dimensionless matchup score (lower is better)', 'O_{\\text{offense}}': 'dimensionless offensive rating'}
primitives.assumptions: Matchup score inversely correlates with offensive strength.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's offensive strength model applied to DST matchups.
layer2.telemetry: Offensive rating of opponent faced by DST.

primitives.assumptions: Projection score scales inversely with salary and directly with edge.

layer2.mapping: GSI's normalized projection kernel adjusted for salary constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Projected edge score weighted by DK salary.

The DST breadth operator models the number of defensive units available for selection against a fixed set of games. It establishes a baseline for coverage and variance in the slate. The offense matchup score is derived from empirical data on offensive ratings, forming a kernel for evaluating DST vulnerability. The salary-weighted projection integrates edge scores with salary constraints to optimize lineup construction. These primitives form a dual structure: one for breadth and one for depth, enabling a robust probabilistic inference engine that accounts for both quantity and quality of DST candidates. Failure modes include overfitting to single-source projections and ignoring weather or injury impacts.
